content:
Hi all — I've formalized the three-gap (Steinhaus / three-distance) theorem in Lean: for irrational α and any N, the points {k·α} for k < N split the circle into arcs taking at most three distinct lengths.

As far as I can tell this is the first formalization in Lean/Mathlib — it's in Coq (Mayero, TYPES'99) but I couldn't find it in Mathlib, Isabelle's AFP, or Metamath. The proof follows Liang's rigid-gap argument (Discrete Math. 28 (1979) 325–326), working with the concrete representatives Int.fract (k·α) ∈ [0,1) (a LinearOrder, so the sorted point set and its gaps come from Finset.orderEmbOfFin). The main result

three_gap : (Finset.univ.image (gap hα)).card ≤ 3

is sorry-free; #print axioms reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

I've opened it as a draft PR: #40037 (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ThreeGapTheorem.lean).

Two questions: (1) is anyone already working on this, and would Mathlib want it? (2) any preference on placement — NumberTheory vs Dynamics?

Disclosure: developed with AI assistance; everything is machine-checked by Lean and axiom-audited as above. Happy to walk through any part or adjust to conventions.
